title: Repricing a Protection Plan to the Recorded Price of Its Covered Holding
content:
The premium on a Pass and Trip Protection plan whose covered value is brought onto the price the covered
holding's own record shows is worked out afresh and replaces the premium frozen on the plan.

**The new covered value.** The price the covered holding's record shows stands as the new covered value only
where it falls between the plan's smallest and largest covered values; where it falls outside them the value
the plan already covers stands and the premium is worked out on that instead.

**The premium at the new value.** The premium at the new value is the plan's rate of the price the covered
holding's record shows — that is, the plan's rate taken of the value the plan now covers — brought up to the
plan's smallest premium where it falls below it and down to the plan's largest premium where it rises above
it, and rounded to the cent; the bounds are applied after the rate and never before.

**What falls due.** The whole difference between the premium at the new value and the premium frozen on the
plan falls due at once.

**The repriced premium.** The repriced premium is the premium frozen on the plan plus the difference that so
falls due, rounded to the cent at the end and at no earlier step.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).** Take a plan whose rate of the value covered is 6.50 per cent, whose
smallest premium is 49.00 USD and largest 195.00 USD, whose covered values run from 559.00 USD to 2649.00 USD,
and which carries a premium frozen at 58.50 USD. The covered holding's record shows a price of 1200.00 USD.
That price falls inside the plan's covered values, so it stands as the new covered value. The plan's rate
taken of it is 78.00 USD, which falls between the smallest and the largest premium and so stands at 78.00 USD
once rounded to the cent. The difference between 78.00 USD and the premium frozen on the plan is 19.50 USD,
and the whole of it falls due at once. The repriced premium is 58.50 USD plus 19.50 USD, which is 78.00 USD.

**Two boundary illustrations (hypothetical inputs).** On the same plan, a covered holding whose record shows a
price of 3000.00 USD falls above the plan's largest covered value, so the value the plan already covers —
900.00 USD, say — stands instead; the plan's rate taken of it is 58.50 USD, the difference is nothing, and the
repriced premium is 58.50 USD. On a plan whose smallest premium is 49.00 USD, a rate taken of the new covered
value that comes to 30.00 USD falls below that floor, so the premium at the new value is brought up to 49.00
USD after the rate has been taken and never before it.
